comments.text: cory you should really try this game Omori. OMORI is a 2020 role-playing video game developed by the indie studio OMOCAT and published by PLAYISM. It's a psychological horror game that follows Sunny, a nonverbal teenage boy who retreats into his dream world after a traumatic event. Players explore both Sunny's real life in Faraway Town and his dream world, Headspace, as Omori, Sunny's alter ego. The game deals with themes of trauma, depression, anxiety, and mental health, impacting Sunny's well-being and how he interacts with his friends. The game features a turn-based battle system where characters' emotions influence their stats, and players' choices lead to different endings.

comments.text: I doubt Cory will see this, but I gotta talk about Monsters We Make bro. I preordered it, so I got it quite some time ago, but I didn’t start reading it until today. The reason I didn’t start reading it is because I wanted to wait until I had finished the Berserk deluxe editions that I had, planning to start monsters we make after Volume 4 of Berserk. I finished volume 4 yesterday and woke up feeling sick today. This happened relatively often, as I have pretty bad acid reflux. Normally, when my reflux hits, I take a warm bath because it seems to soothe my stomach. This morning, when I was about to walk to the bathroom to take a nice, warm bath, I spotted out of the corner of my eye, Monsters We Make. Naturally, having finished the berserk deluxe edition volumes I had, I decided it’d be the perfect time to pick up MWM and read the first chapter, so I got into the bath and began reading. I finished the first chapter… and then moved onto the second, then the third, you get the idea. The fact that I went into it saying “yeah I’ll read a chapter” and then just read the ENTIRE first volume in one sitting speaks volumes to me. I had high hopes for MWM, but I didn’t expect it to hook me as easily and as effortlessly as it did. Again, I doubt Cory will see this, but incredible work‼️

comments.text:
Cory I PROMISE hard mode has an awesome story! It continues from the normal modes ending but you have to do the entire run without dying in the car irl (if you die in the game it just forfeits your items). I have some tips too to make it more fair on your next run:

Bear traps are an item you CAN pick up, you can place them in the car alongside the cardboard baracades for extra protection. The demon will break the glass first, then it will get you if you're not fast enough; use the cardboard to replace the glass as a barrier. The soda speeds up the car giving you a few seconds without any attacks to refresh your defences, but I think you can still hit obstacles in the mini-game. I think whilst your in the scavenging mini-game's dialogue cutscenes you can flip down the Game Kyd for unlimited time to set up the traps and baracades! Good luck!
